source_name: ISPV — Informační systém o průměrném výdělku (TREXIMA for MPSV)
why_relevant: Semi-annual earnings survey by CZ-ISCO occupation and CZ-NACE, published as downloadable PDFs/tables including the wage sphere. Lets you track pay and staffing structure for banking occupations (tellers, advisors, IT) — an early indicator of role-mix shifts, offshoring and branch-staff attrition. Note ČSÚ takes over wage-structure processing from reference year 2026 (JMHZ), so the series may migrate.

source_name: Česká národní banka — banking statistics (bank & branch network counts)
why_relevant: ČNB is the authoritative counter of banks and their branch/business-place networks; media consistently cite ČNB data for branch-closure trends (peak 2013, subsequent decline). Branch-network shrinkage is the physical footprint of the org change unions comment on.

source_name: Eurofound European Restructuring Monitor (ERM) — restructuring events database
why_relevant: EU-wide, daily-updated factsheet database of restructuring events with ≥100 jobs affected (or ≥10% of a 250+ establishment), covering CZ. Contains concrete Czech banking factsheets (e.g. ING Bank Czech Republic closure, 225 jobs, 2021). Structured, comparable, and explicitly job-count oriented — the best cross-border benchmark for CZ bank downsizing.

source_name: UNI Europa Finance (and UNI Global Union) — finance sector federation
why_relevant: European federation to which finance-sector unions affiliate; runs a Central Europe Organising Centre covering CZ/PL/SK/HU and publishes on bank restructuring, transnational consultation and cross-border bargaining (BARSERVICE project). Surfaces group-level restructurings (Erste, KBC, SocGen, UniCredit) whose Czech subsidiaries are affected before local disclosure.

source_name: Veřejný rejstřík / spolkový rejstřík (justice.cz) — registrations of ZO OS union organisations at banks
why_relevant: Each basic union organisation (ZO OS pracovníků peněžnictví a pojišťovnictví <bank name>) is a registered legal entity with its own IČO, seat and statutory representatives. Registrations, address changes and dissolutions are an indirect but hard signal of union presence, mergers of bank entities, and site/branch consolidation. Mirrors (podnikatel.cz, rejstrik.penize.cz, kurzy.cz, finmag.cz) are easier to search by name.

source_name: Seznam Zprávy — banking layoffs / restructuring reporting
why_relevant: Major CZ news outlet that has broken concrete bank workforce-reduction numbers (e.g. Komerční banka reducing from ~7,340 to ~5,500 staff over five years). Business desk regularly sources union and internal-memo material that banks do not publish.

Business daily that reports union reactions directly — e.g. ČSOB union organisations formally objecting in writing to announced layoffs. HN is the outlet unions use to escalate; the archive gives multi-year continuity on bank restructuring rounds.

Consistently covers Czech bank headcount cuts and branch closures with named figures and rationale (digitalisation, management simplification, IT rehiring). Good structured feed for the 'firms quietly cut, media report' pattern.

Analytical weekly covering the 'cut hard but quietly' pattern across ČS, ČSOB and KB — explicitly framing bank savings plans and layoffs that are not formally announced, and flagging union bargaining ahead.

Regional dailies routinely report ÚP regional-branch statements about mass-redundancy notifications and local employer closures — often the ONLY public trace of a specific notification, including where a bank's back-office or regional site is affected. Complements national coverage that ignores small towns where branches actually close.

source_name: Peníze.cz — bank branch-count rankings and branch-closure tracking
why_relevant: Maintains a recurring, comparable ranking of Czech banks by branch and cash-desk count (e.g. ČS 329 branches early 2026 vs 369 in Aug 2023 vs 400+ in early 2021; KB 185, down 18 y/y). A ready-made, per-bank time series of network shrinkage that ČNB aggregates do not give at firm level.
A pre-built, continuously updated tag feed for layoffs across the Czech economy — a low-cost pointer stream to filter for finance-sector events without running many queries.

Union social channels often carry faster, blunter statements about a specific bank's redundancy round than the website, plus recruitment drives at newly-unionising employers. Useful for real-time signal, weak for archival reliability.
Ostrava is CZ's #3 business-services hub (49 centres, heavy finance/accounting share). This edition reports SSC openings, shared-workspace moves and local employer hiring before national media.
Brno hosts a large concentration of banking/finance shared-service and IT centres; the local Deník edition covers new employer arrivals, headcount announcements and office moves.
Hradec Králové is named by ABSL among cities hosting business-services centres; local Deník edition is the only outlet likely to report a bank back-office site there.

source_name: Magazín PATRIOT / PATRIOT Zprávy — Byznys section (Moravia & Silesia)
why_relevant: Independent Ostrava-based business news outlet with a dedicated Byznys rubric; covers regional employers, office/centre openings and management changes in Moravia-Silesia that national media skip.
Regional TV newsroom for the MS region; carries city/employer press-conference coverage (job creation, investor arrivals) with video, often the first record of a local announcement.
Regional news + company directory + job listings aggregator for Ostrava/MS kraj; low editorial value but useful as a cheap sweep of local hiring notices.
Brno/Jihomoravský kraj news, company catalogue and vacancy listings; a secondary sweep layer for local employer hiring outside the big job boards.
Aggregates regional press coverage and local job ads (incl. náborový příspěvek offers) for Královéhradecký kraj — a pointer into smaller outlets in a region otherwise invisible.
Small free regional paper/portal; carries employer profiles and hiring features that never reach national media.

The dominant Czech employee-review platform. Reviews name reorganisations, new management, front-vs-back-office pay gaps, turnover and layoff fear — the earliest, cheapest signal of internal change at CZ banks, months before any filing or press release. Per-employer statistics pages give trend lines.

source_name: Atmoskop employer-entity ID pattern (pointer to full CZ bank/fintech roster)
why_relevant: Each employer has a stable numeric ID + slug (e.g. 2946946-ceska-sporitelna-a-s, 2992632-...-penzijni-spolecnost). Enumerating IDs for every bank, its subsidiaries, payment institutions and their SSC entities builds the actor map for the whole A5 workstream.

Captures the English-speaking SSC/GBS workforce in Brno and Ostrava — expat and international-team staff who describe reorganisations, site ramp-ups/ramp-downs and new country managers in English, complementing cs-only Atmoskop.

source_name: Indeed Czech Republic — company reviews & regional job listings
why_relevant: Two signals in one: (a) company review pages for CZ banks, (b) geo-filtered vacancy counts per employer per region — a rising Brno/Ostrava req count for a bank is the leading indicator of a back-office build-out. Observed listing counts for 'Banka' in Brno grew across snapshots.

source_name: Jobs.cz — Banking & financial services, regional filters (LMC/Alma Career)
why_relevant: The primary CZ white-collar board; region+sector filtered URLs give a clean per-kraj banking vacancy series. Job titles reveal new team/function names (e.g. a new 'shared services' or 'hub' unit) before any announcement.
Sister board to Jobs.cz aimed at mass-market/branch roles; branch-banker req volumes per city are a proxy for retail network expansion or contraction outside Prague.

Aggregates across boards including small local ones, so it surfaces vacancies that never appear on Jobs.cz; per-employer+city URLs (Komerční banka/Brno, ČSOB/Brno) make actor-level regional monitoring cheap.
Smaller CZ board with clean sector+city URL structure; useful as a third independent count to sanity-check Jobs.cz/Indeed regional hiring trends.
